verdict.rationale: The Agent Server (the LangGraph Platform runtime, which the LangGraph CLI builds and runs) publishes an OpenAPI spec that includes a 'Crons' endpoint group, so recurring scheduled runs are a first-party capability. The evidence only names that endpoint group, with no description of cron syntax, management, or behavior. It also appears tied to the server/deployment layer rather than the open-source graph library. Community mentions of 'scheduling' refer to execution scheduling inside the framework, not recurring jobs, so they are not credited. Missing for 10: documentation of how cron jobs are created and managed, schedule syntax and limits, clarity on availability outside the platform runtime, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: covering Assistants ("An assistant is a configured instance of a graph."), Threads, Thread Runs, Stateless Runs, Crons, Store, A2A, MCP, and System endpoints
LangGraph CLI is a command-line tool for building and running the Agent Server locally. The resulting server exposes all API endpoints for runs, threads, assistants, etc.
